MINUTES
  MALIBU PUBLIC SAFETY COMMISSION
  REGULAR MEETING
  SEPTEMBER 7, 2022
  TELECONFERENCED VARIOUS LOCATIONS
  -

  5:00 P.M.

The following meeting was held pursuant to AB 361 and fully teleconferenced from various
locations during the coronavirus disease (COVID-19) pandemic.

CALL TO ORDER

  Chair Frost called the meeting to order at 5:01 p.m.

ROLL CALL

  The following persons were recorded in attendance by the Recording Secretary:

  PRESENT: Chair Chris Frost; Vice Chair Doug Stewart; Commissioners Daphne Anneet,
  and Joshua Spiegel; and Ex Officio Member Brent Woodworth

  ABSENT:  Commissioner Keegan Gibbs

  ALSO PRESENT:  Rob DuBoux, Public Works Director; Luis Flores, Public Safety
  Liaison, Sarah Kaplan, Emergency Services Coordinator; Gabe Etcheverry, Fire Safety
  Liaison; Greg Hisel, Fire Safety Liaison; Brad Yocum, Fire Safety Liaison; Parker Davis,
  Media Technician; Lieutenant Dustin Carr, Los Angeles County Sheriff’s Department; and
  Mary Linden, Executive Assistant

PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE

  Public Safety Liaison Flores led the Pledge of Allegiance.

APPROVAL OF AGENDA

MOTION  Commissioner Spiegel moved, and Vice Chair Stewart seconded a motion to
  approve the agenda. The question was called, and the motion carried 4-0,
  Commissioner Gibbs absent.

REPORT ON POSTING OF AGENDA

  Executive Assistant Linden reported that the agenda for the meeting was properly posted
  on September 1, 2022.

ITEM 1  CEREMONIAL / PRESENTATIONS

  None.

ITEM 2.A.  PUBLIC COMMENTS

  Matt Winter was unavailable at the time of the hearing.

ITEM 2.B.  STAFF UPDATES

  Public Works Director DuBoux discussed road closures for the Malibu Triathlon
  scheduled next weekend. He stated crews worked the Labor Day weekend, clearing
  trash and assisting with a traffic accident. He stated he was trying to schedule a
  joint Public Safety Commission and Public Works Commission meeting to discuss
  Caltrans projects.

  Emergency Services Coordinator Kaplan discussed the Ride to the Flags
  motorcycle event on Saturday, September 10. She stated participants would arrive
  at Bluffs Park in Malibu between 10:00 a.m. and 11:00 a.m. She announced a CERT
  Team meeting and events planned for Malibu Preparedness Month. She stated test
  emergency alerts were being sent weekly by evacuation zone.

  Public Safety Liaison Flores stated impound yard towed 63 vehicles over Labor
  Day weekend, for a total of 293 vehicles towed since the operation began on June
  18. He stated the lot would be used through October 3. He announced Homelessness
  Connect Day on September 22. He stated the County’s Homeless Count numbers
  would be provided soon. He stated the Commission’s recommendation about Knox
  boxes would be presented to the City Council on September 12. He stated Public
  Safety staff were working proactively with outreach team and other agencies to
  keep hillsides and canyons clear of encampments in advance of fire season.

  Chair Frost stated the updated number of towed vehicles was 75 cars for the holiday
  weekend.

  Fire Safety Liaison Yocum stated 30 Home Ignition Zone Assessments were
  completed so far this year. He stated he would teach home hardening classes on
  September 21 and 28. He stated Live Fuel Moisture (LFM) remained at critical
  levels and was down 63% to 69% with a burn index of 114. He discussed a small
  fire about up Corral Canyon last Friday in an abandoned building.

  Fire Safety Liaison Hisel announced he would host a earthquake preparedness class
  on September 19 in preparation for the Great Shakeout on October 20.

  Emergency Services Coordinator Kaplan stated there were two home hardening
  classes with one virtual and one in-person.

  Chair Frost reopened Item No. 2.A.

ITEM 2.A.  PUBLIC COMMENTS

  Matt Winter, Sierra Towing, thanked the City for allowing his company to use the
  City’s impound lot. He discussed the service provided from Zuma Beach to
  Surfrider Beach. He stated having a fenced yard so close was a great benefit. He
  stated there was confusion in the public about the emergency order.

ITEM 2.C.  COMMISSIONER COMMENTS

  Ex Officio Member Woodworth stated he was working with insurance industry
  representatives about urban interface fire risk analysis using satellite data. He
  discussed a meeting with the Los Angeles County Fire Department about
  community brigades. He discussed funding available to Caltrans that could be used
  for improvements at the PCH/Las Flores Canyon Road intersection.

  Commissioner Anneet commended staff for their work for National Preparedness
  Month and the diversity of programming. She suggested promoting the events on
  social media. She urged Commissioners to share the information.

  Commissioner Spiegel thanked Ex Officio Member Woodworth for his work on the
  brigades. He stated earthquake preparedness was important. He stated Malibu
  residents were woefully unprepared for a potential loss of water in an emergency.
  He stated he attended the Chili Cook-Off. He stated the lot next door was previously
  used for parking but not this year, which led to an unsafe situation. He suggested
  there be more lights and better traffic control next year. He discussed previous
  meetings and recommendations about Westward Beach. He stated there was no
  signage on PCH alerting motorists when the lots were full. He suggested a solution
  for next summer be placed on an upcoming agenda.

  Vice Chair Stewart discussed Labor Day including fatal accident, closed beaches,
  Chili Cook-Off. He asked what would have happened if evacuations had been
  necessary. He suggested an after action review be included in an upcoming agenda.
  In response to Vice Chair Stewart, Executive Assistant Linden stated these issues
  could be discussed during the annual review of public safety services at the October
  meeting. zones. In response to Vice Chair Stewart, Emergency Services
  Coordinator Kaplan stated evacuation zones were finalized and were uploaded into
  the City’s emergency notification system. She stated the City was waiting for the
  County’s media campaign announcing the updates. She stated there were minimal
  changes to the City’s evacuation zones. In response to Vice Chair Stewart, Public
  Safety Liaison Flores stated automatic license plate readers (ALPR) cameras were
  ordered in July but not yet shipped. In response to Vice Chair Stewart, Public
  Works Director DuBoux stated Botts dots were being installed throughout the City.
  He requested specific locations where they were missing be sent to staff. Vice Chair

  Stewart agreed with Commissioner Anneet that staff did a great job on Emergency
  Preparedness Month.

  In response to Vice Chair Stewart, Chair Frost stated the new Volunteers on Patrol
  (VOP) car bailment agreement had to be rerouted for updated City signatures. He
  stated it would be equipped after the agreement was finalized. He discussed the
  State and County fireworks ordinances. He suggested the City have a fireworks
  ordinance and fee schedule. Executive Assistant Linden stated she would send a
  copy of the City’s ordinance. He stated there were too many trucks on PCH and
  Kanan Dume Road. He suggested the restriction on large trucks be more strongly
  enforced. He discussed electronic ticket writers bought by the City for use by
  Sheriffs deputies. He agreed with Commissioner Spiegel about illegal parking and
  other safety concerns at Westward Beach. He expressed disappointment in the
  community’s response to recommended solutions. He stated he looked forward to
  meeting with the Public Works Commission again on solutions. He discussed road
  racing on PCH. He questioned why there was no Sheriff presence. He discussed
  dry, crisp brush in Latigo Canyon that was a serious fire hazard. In response to Mr.
  Winter, he agreed illegal parking was a mini-emergency. He commended the
  towing company for their tremendous work over the holiday weekend.

ITEM 3  CONSENT CALENDAR

MOTION  Vice Chair Stewart moved, and Chair Frost seconded a motion to approve the
  Consent Calendar. The question was called, and the motion carried 4-0,

  The Consent Calendar consisted of the following items:

ITEM 5  NEW BUSINESS

  A.  Day-Use Impound Site
  Recommended Action: Develop plans for selecting a temporary site for a day-use
  impound yard in Summer 2023 and identifying potential locations for a permanent
  impound site.

  Executive Assistant Linden presented the report.

  Chair Frost stated he and Commissioner Spiegel spoke with many in the community
  who stated the situation was far better than they expected.

  Commissioner Spiegel stated he and Chair Frost started looking for locations in
  October 2021. He discussed the time necessary for permitting. He discussed the
  process needed to find a temporary site for next summer and a permanent location.

  Executive Assistant Linden stated the City had not yet scheduled community
  meetings to discuss the uses of the City’s vacant properties.

  Chair Frost stated the emergency ordinance restricted the use of the Heathercliff lot
  to this year only. He explained the number of cars in the lot at any one time did not
  indicate the number of cars towed on that day.

  Commissioner Spiegel stated he agreed the City needed a permanent impound yard,
  and a temporary site for summer months needed to be considered as well. He stated
  he valued community involvement, but it should not delay this process. He
  requested feedback from the Sheriff’s Department and the tow company about what
  did and did not work this summer. He suggested forming an ad hoc committee.

  Chair Frost stated the majority of vehicles were towed from western Malibu. He
  stated the previous tow company could not efficiently service the entire city with a
  tow yard in central Malibu. He stated a western Malibu location would be most
  efficient. He stated the Heathercliff location was ideal.

  Commissioner Anneet stated communication was very important. She stated full
  transparency and understanding needed to include what options were considered
  and how a decision was made. She commended Chair Frost and Commissioner
  Spiegel for their efforts last year. She asked if it was possible to get a list of City
  properties that could be considered and whether there were private properties that
  could be considered. She stated cost of the property could be factored into the cost
  of the tow. She requested a summary report, including where tows initiated, be
  provided with the end of summer reports. She suggested safety considerations of
  each location be provided. She expressed concern about people safely walking from
  where their cars were towed to collect them at the impound yard.

  Chair Frost requested a copy of the list of zoned properties provided by the previous
  City Manager be re-sent.

  Commissioner Anneet discussed the end of the Zuma Beach parking lot that was
  seldom used. She asked if flatbed trucks could go through the underpass off Busch
  Drive at Zuma Beach. In response to Commissioner Anneet, Chair Frost stated the
  problem was getting trucks in and out during busy summer weekends.

  Ex Officio Member Woodworth agreed with Commissioner Spiegel and
  Commissioner Anneet. He stated having a list of detailed criteria, including space,
  access, safety, environmental impacts, noise, and pollution, was important. He
  agreed with including private properties that could be leased by the City.

  Chair Frost stated the equestrian center had been considered, but it was usually used
  on weekends. In response to Chair Frost, Commissioner Spiegel stated the school
  district had a plan to use the equestrian center as a bus barn.

  Vice Chair Stewart stated the concept had been proven successful twice. He
  discussed how moving illegally parked vehicles was critical in case of an
  emergency. He stated the Heathercliff site was a perfect choice. He stated the City
  had said it would not use the site again. He stated the bus barn plan at the equestrian
  center was only a consideration. He suggested the Commission submit a formal
  report to the Council about the impound yard this summer. He discussed properties
  that were commercially zoned that would not be valid options.

  Commissioner Anneet stated she would volunteer to assist with identifying sites.

MOTION  Commissioner Spiegel moved, and Chair Frost seconded a motion to: 1) form an
  Impound Yard Ad Hoc Committee to explore sites for a permanent impound yard
  and a Summer 2023 temporary impound yard; and 2) appoint Commissioner
  Spiegel and Commissioner Anneet to the ad hoc committee. The question was
  called, and the motion carried 4-0, Commissioner Gibbs absent.

  B.  Public Safety Agency Activity
  Recommended Action: Discuss recent Public Safety Agency activities and receive
  and file activity reports from the County of Los Angeles Sheriff’s Department, Fire
  Department, and Lifeguard Division.

  Lieutenant Carr discussed fireworks explosions during the nights of August 26 and
  August 27. He stated a crime report was taken and juveniles were identified. He
  requested reports of street racers be emailed to him. He stated the Lost Hills
  Homelessness Liaison Deputy and Homeless Outreach Services Team (HOST)
  found no new encampments in Las Tunas Canyon. He stated a homeless pregnant
  female was provided a ticket home to reconnect with her family, another individual

  was housed, and another approved for a housing voucher. He discussed quick
  response to incidents at the Chili Cook-Off. He stated the final Beach Team report
  would be presented to the City Council on September 12. He discussed a single-
  vehicle fatal rollover on Malibu Canyon on September 4. He reported there were
  no fatal collisions in July or August. He announced Coffee with a Cop at the Malibu
  Farmers Market on Sunday, September 18, from 10:00 a.m. to 1:00 p.m.

  In response to Chair Frost, Lieutenant Carr stated he would follow up on the ticket
  writers tomorrow. Lieutenant Carr stated another recreational vehicle (RV)
  operation would be scheduled later this month.

  Chair Frost stated enforcement needed to be more consistent. Chair Frost stated the
  City bought four LIDAR guns last year for deputies to enforce street racers.

ADJOURNMENT

MOTION  At 6:36 p.m., Vice Chair Stewart moved, and Commissioner Spiegel seconded a
  motion to adjourn the meeting. The question was called, and the motion carried 4-
  0, Commissioner Gibbs absent.
